props.title: OpenHarness for ==Windows==
props.subtitle: The AI agent command center, now on Windows.

slides.notes: Open the hook: OpenHarness gives you one command center for every AI coding agent you run. This deck is about bringing it to Windows.

props.title: Two platforms supported. One left out.

left.label: Ships today
left.title: Mac & Linux
points: Open-source command center for running AI agents across machines
Harness Pro desk screen — 720×720 touch display for watching agents

right.label: Left out
right.title: Windows
points: No daemon, no desk screen support
A large share of working developers can't run the stack
Watching agents means reaching for a second machine

slides.notes: Frame the problem: OpenHarness and the Harness Pro desk screen both ship Mac and Linux only. Windows developers are structurally excluded.

props.title: ==Full hosting== on Windows — via WSL2.
props.body: The real OpenHarness daemon, running natively on Windows machines through WSL2. Not a stripped-down viewer.

slides.notes: Key design decision: this is not a thin client or dashboard pointed at a Mac. The daemon itself runs on Windows, under WSL2.

props.caption: commits covering platform detection, process & terminal handling, and the security-sensitive launch paths — contributed back upstream as draft PR #1389

slides.notes: Scope of the port in one number. Emphasize that all of it goes back upstream as draft PR #1389 — it is a contribution, not a private fork.

stats.label: Typecheck
stats.caption: No type errors across the port

stats.label: Failures forced
stats.caption: Remaining failures are documented and deliberately left unforced

slides.notes: Be straight here: 247 targeted specs pass and typecheck is clean. The remaining failures are documented and deliberately left unforced. A full on-Windows test run is the next verification step — it has not happened yet.

tiles.title: WSL2 hosting
tiles.body: The full daemon runs on Windows hardware — agents live where you work.
